title: Infectious disease doctor visit
what: A doctor who treats infections caused by viruses, bacteria, or parasites, and helps with vaccines before travel.
why: For a long-lasting fever, gut infections, hepatitis, abnormal infection tests, after travel abroad, or after a tick bite.
tell_doctor: When the fever started and how it changed
Where you traveled in recent months
Contact with sick people, or tick or animal bites
What medicines you took, including antibiotics

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring all your test results, if you had any.

prepare.title: Temperature
prepare.text: Write down how your temperature changed day by day.

prepare.title: Mask
prepare.text: If you have a fever or cough, wear a mask and tell the front desk.

bring: Your vaccination certificate, if you have one
Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms, travel, and contacts
Your skin, throat, and lymph nodes are checked
feel: Nothing unpleasant. It is a regular checkup
Sometimes blood or a swab is taken the same day
after: Have the tests done and come back with the results
Take antibiotics only as prescribed, and finish the course
red_flags: A very high fever, confusion, or a rash that does not fade when pressed: call emergency services

faq.q: Should I see a doctor after a tick bite?
faq.a: Yes, it is best to. You can keep the tick for testing. Check with the clinic.

faq.q: Why does the doctor ask about travel?
faq.a: Different countries have different infections. It helps find the cause.

reminders.text: Infectious disease visit tomorrow. Bring your test results, and recall your recent travel and contacts.
